decision_rule: Per family, Cochran-Armitage-style trend: pre-registered one-sided test of whether P(harden beats rigid at 1e-4) increases with n across the pooled instances (C01 n=5..8 + C02a + C07 n=9..11 for that family). Report per-instance bests and gaps regardless.
hypothesis: The harden advantage grows with piece count within concave families (more pieces -> more interlocking -> more steric barriers for rigid search).
question: Does the hardening advantage grow with n?
title: Concave n-scaling
